subject: Estimator for MIMIC-Modell with binary exogenous variables

messages.author: 1f2686cf8a9955b7
messages.subject: Estimator for MIMIC-Modell with binary exogenous variables
parts:
Dear Mr. Rosseel,

I’d be extremely thankful for your advice which estimator to use in a specific situation.

My aim is to validate a formative construct. Following Diamantopoulos, Winklhuber 2001, p. 272 or Jarvis, MacKenzie, Podsakoff 2003, p. 213 (pdfs attached) I specified the following simple MIMIC-model:

F = Latent Variable
y1, y2 = reflective Items
x1, x2, x3, x4 = formative Items

MIMIC <- '# MIMIC Model
                # reflective part
                   F =~ y1 + y2
                # formative part
                   F <~ 1*x1 + x2 + x3 + x4
                # Intercept
                   F ~ 0
                # Error on level of the LV
                   F ~~ NA*F
                # Item-level error 
                   y1 ~~ NA*y1
                   y2 ~~ NA*y2’

My difficulty is the following: the formative Items are binary. In this situation, I do not know which estimator to use. I used WLSMV until I read that binary variables do not need any special treatment as long as they are exogenous. So I tried ML. The estimation works, but then for x1, x2, x3, x4 covariances, intercepts, and variances are not estimated anymore. What is the reason?

I am afraid, I am missing something very fundamental here. I can’t find the solution, although studying the literature.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Estimator for MIMIC-Modell with binary exogenous variables
parts:
Apologies to Diamantopoulos et al., but the model looks underidentified to me.  Scale your F as for a reflective model, by fixings loading (for y1 or y2) to 1.  Then try it.  Fixing a regression weight to 1 will not have the same effect.
--Ed Rigdon

Dear Edward,

Thank you for your answer. You are absolutely right, the model should look like this:

F =~ 1*y1 + y2

# formative part

                # Intercept
                   F ~ 0
                # Error on level of the LV
                   F ~~ NA*F
                # Item-level error 
                   y1 ~~ NA*y1
                   y2 ~~ NA*y2’

Nevertheless, in the estimation step, lavaan fixed the first loading to 1 per default, although it was not specified explicitly. So on this side everything should be ok.

My problem deals with the fact that the model output differs, depending on the estimator used. I should specify my questions:
1. Estimator choice: Which is the appropriate estimator in this situation (binary exogenous variables, continuous endogenous variables)?
2. Covariances of exogenous variables: Why are they not part of the ML estimation results? How are they estimated with WLSMV? They are not explained by the model, or am I wrong?

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Estimator for MIMIC-Modell with binary exogenous variables
parts:
On 11/21/2015 09:14 PM, Juliet wrote:
> My problem deals with the fact that the model output differs, depending
> on the estimator used. I should specify my questions:
> 1. Estimator choice: Which is the appropriate estimator in this
> situation (binary exogenous variables, continuous endogenous variables)?

Only the endogenous variables matter. If they are all continuous, go for
ML or MLR.

> 2. Covariances of exogenous variables: Why are they not part of the ML
> estimation results?

Because -by default- they are considered as 'fixed' (just like in
regression). If you prefer stochastic x-variables, use fixed.x = FALSE.
> How are they estimated with WLSMV?

It depends. In 0.5-20, if you only have continuous endogenous variables,
WLS and friends will treat the x-variables as stochastic (unlike ML). If
you have categorical endogenous variables, WLS will use a conditional
model and condition on the 'x' variables.

Yves.
